prompt: Produce exactly one concise natural‑language caption (a single sentence) that vividly and precisely describes the main subject(s), visible actions and interactions, and the setting; remain concrete, image‑centered and avoid speculation or subjective judgments. For every person and object state whether it is stationary or moving; when describing motion give horizontal direction first then vertical relative to the image frame (for example, "from left to right," "toward the camera while descending"), name the visible motion phase when apparent (starting/ascending/peaking/descending/landing), and indicate whether motions are simultaneous or sequential. For each moving subject describe trajectory both relative to the main subject (passing to his right, approaching from behind, moving alongside) and relative to the camera (toward the camera, away from the camera, to the left/right edge of the frame); ensure every visible pedestrian or figure’s movement direction is specified from the camera’s perspective. Specify each person’s head orientation and gaze precisely (for example, "looking directly at the camera," "eyes down at a phone," "gaze up and left," "head turned slightly right while facing forward") to clarify focus. For interactions with objects or structures state exactly how the subject is using them (holding/gripping/resting/leaning/pushing), which hand and side (left/right), and whether the hand is in contact, gripping, merely near, in motion, or resting. Describe body posture with concrete camera‑relative terms (standing upright, weight on left leg, slightly leaning forward, seated, crouching, mid‑jump, arms outstretched) and specify orientation to the camera (facing the camera, in profile, back to the camera); indicate whether the subject is centered or offset in the frame. Clarify precise spatial relationships, counts, arrangement, proximity and relative scale using camera‑relative language and clear phrases (foreground/midground/background; left/middle/right of frame; directly in front of/behind; clustered closely; a few feet/meters apart). Describe lighting, shadows and visible surface textures with observable cues and note absence of distinct shadows or even diffuse illumination when applicable (for example, "bright direct sunlight casting long shadows toward the lower left," "diffuse overcast with minimal shadows," "wet pavement reflecting light"). Report facial expressions or visible affect only when clearly evident using observable detail (for example, "smiling with teeth visible," "furrowed brow"). Keep the caption concise, factual and single‑sentence. Output exactly one single sentence.
